subject: Maths
title: Vector geometry proofs
subtitle: Vectors · GCSE Maths
learning_objective: I can use vectors to prove geometric results involving midpoints, parallel lines, and collinear points.

key_vocab.definition: In vector geometry, we express journeys around a shape in terms of vectors a and b. If two vectors are parallel (scalar multiples), the lines are parallel.

sections.title: Learning Objective
sections.content: I can use vectors to prove geometric results involving midpoints, parallel lines, and collinear points.

sections.title: Key Words
sections.content: vector geometry -- In vector geometry, we express journeys around a shape in terms of vectors a and b. If two vectors are parallel (scalar multiples), the lines are parallel.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
Express unknown vectors as journeys using known vectors. Parallel means scalar multiple; collinear needs shared point too.
AB = b - a
Travel from A to O (which is -a), then O to B (which is +b)

Key examples:
  ✓ AB = b - a (position vectors)  (from A to B)
  ✓ Midpoint M of AB: OM = &frac{1}{2}(a + b)  (average of position vectors)
  ✓ If PQ = kRS, then PQ is parallel to RS  (scalar multiple means parallel)
  ✗ AB = a + b  (should be b - a)
  ✗ Parallel vectors prove collinearity  (also need a shared point)

sections.title: Worked Example
sections.content:
Example 1 – expressing a vector
  OA = a, OB = b. Express AB in terms of a and b.
  AB = AO + OB
  AO = -a (reverse of OA)
  AB = -a + b = b - a
  AB = b - a
  (Go backwards along a, then forwards along b.)

Example 2 – finding a midpoint
  M is the midpoint of AB. OA = a, OB = b. Find OM.
  OM = OA + AM
  AM = &frac{1}{2}AB = &frac{1}{2}(b - a)
  OM = a + &frac{1}{2}(b - a) = &frac{1}{2}(a + b)
  OM = &frac{1}{2}(a + b)
  (The midpoint is the average of the position vectors.)

sections.title: Expressing vectors
sections.content:
OA = a, OB = b. Express in terms of a and b.

(a) AB
(b) BA
(c) 2OA + OB
(d) OA + &frac{1}{2}AB

sections.title: Midpoints
sections.content:
Find the position vector of the midpoint M.

(a) OA = (2, 6), OB = (4, 8). M midpoint of AB.
(b) OA = (1, 3), OB = (5, 7). M midpoint of AB.
(c) OA = a, OB = b. M midpoint of AB.
(d) OA = (0, 4), OB = (6, 0). M midpoint of AB.

sections.title: Proving parallel lines
sections.content:
Show that the vectors are parallel.

(a) PQ = 2a + b, RS = 6a + 3b
(b) AB = a - 2b, CD = 3a - 6b
(c) EF = 4a + 2b, GH = 2a + b
(d) MN = -a + 3b, PQ = 2a - 6b

sections.title: Ratio problems
sections.content:
P divides AB in the given ratio. Find OP.

(a) OA = a, OB = b. P divides AB in ratio 1:1.
(b) OA = a, OB = b. P divides AB in ratio 1:2.
(c) OA = a, OB = b. P divides AB in ratio 2:1.
(d) OA = (2, 1), OB = (8, 7). P divides AB in ratio 1:2.

sections.title: Mixed vector proofs
sections.content:
Solve each problem.

(a) OA = a, OB = b, OC = a + b. What shape is OACB?
(b) OA = 2a, AB = 6a. Is O, A, B collinear?
(c) OA = a, OB = b, M midpoint of AB. Express OM.
(d) If AB = 3(CD), what can you say about AB and CD?
(e) OA = a, OB = b. X is on AB such that AX:XB = 3:1. Find OX.

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
✓ AB = b - a when OA = a and OB = b
✗ AB = a + b
✓ If PQ = kRS, then PQ and RS are parallel
✗ Parallel vectors always prove collinearity
✓ Midpoint of AB = &frac{1}{2}(a + b) when OA = a, OB = b

teacher_sections.title: Teacher Key & Mark Scheme
teacher_sections.content:
Award marks for correct working and final answers.

Expressing vectors:
  (a) b - a
  (b) a - b
  (c) 2a + b
  (d) &frac{1}{2}(a + b)

Midpoints:
  (a) (3, 7)
  (b) (3, 5)
  (c) &frac{1}{2}(a + b)
  (d) (3, 2)

Proving parallel lines:
  (a) RS = 3(PQ)
  (b) CD = 3(AB)
  (c) EF = 2(GH)
  (d) PQ = -2(MN)

Ratio problems:
  (a) &frac{1}{2}(a + b)
  (b) &frac{2}{3}a + &frac{1}{3}b
  (c) &frac{1}{3}a + &frac{2}{3}b
  (d) (4, 3)

Mixed vector proofs:
  (a) Parallelogram
  (b) Yes (OB = 8a = 4(OA))
  (c) &frac{1}{2}(a + b)
  (d) Parallel, AB is 3 times as long
  (e) &frac{1}{4}a + &frac{3}{4}b
